title: Mirzapur: The Movie — Critics Say Pankaj Tripathi and Ali Fazal Deliver a Thrilling Return to the Underworld
excerpt: Critics are largely positive about the film, praising its engaging narrative and performances despite some concerns over its length.
body:
• Critics praise Pankaj Tripathi's performance as a standout.
  • The film successfully taps into nostalgia for fans of the series.
  • Length and predictability are noted as drawbacks.

Critics are largely positive about Mirzapur: The Movie, praising its engaging narrative and performances despite some concerns over its length. Directed by Gurmmeet Singh, this film serves as a cinematic continuation of the popular web series, diving back into the lawless world of Mirzapur where power struggles and violent confrontations reign supreme. The film features returning favorites like Pankaj Tripathi and Ali Fazal, who reprise their roles in a story that escalates the battle for control of the underworld.

What Critics Are Saying

"Mirzapur: The Movie drops you back into the same rough, lawless world that hooked viewers across three seasons of the show, and for a while, it works." — Times of India
"A solid addition to the Mirzapur franchise that enriches the established universe and hints at future developments in the series timeline." — The Week
"Ali Fazal and Divyenndu bring the testosterone, while Pankaj Tripathi remains the heart of the film." — Bollywood Hungama
"The film is a paisa vasool big-screen entertainer, though its bloated runtime is a drawback." — Film Information
"Mirzapur: The Movie is a nostalgic return that balances fan service with genuine storytelling." — Hollywood Reporter India

What Works

  • Performances: Pankaj Tripathi's portrayal of Kaleen Bhaiya continues to be a standout, with critics highlighting his ability to convey depth and menace. Ali Fazal and Divyenndu also receive praise for their strong performances, bringing energy and intensity to their roles.
  • Direction and Cinematography: Gurmmeet Singh's direction captures the gritty essence of Mirzapur, with well-executed action sequences and a visually compelling aesthetic that enhances the narrative.
  • Nostalgia Factor: The film successfully taps into the nostalgia of fans of the series, delivering familiar characters and settings that resonate well with the audience.

What Doesn't

  • Length: Many critics noted the film's lengthy runtime of 197 minutes, suggesting that it could have benefited from tighter editing to maintain pacing and engagement.
  • Predictability: Some reviews pointed out that while the film delivers on action and drama, certain plot points feel predictable, lacking the surprise twists that characterized the series.

The Verdict

Mirzapur: The Movie is a must-see for fans of the series, offering a thrilling return to a beloved universe with strong performances and engaging storytelling. While its length may deter some viewers, the film's nostalgic appeal and action-packed sequences make it a worthy cinematic experience for the diaspora audience.
